title: Emergent Second Law for Time-Dependent Nonequilibrium States
authors: Nahuel Freitas, Timur Aslyamov, Massimiliano Esposito
abstract: For nonautonomous open systems described by macroscopic stochastic thermodynamics, we derive an emergent second law that constrains time-dependent macroscopic fluctuations by the entropy production along the most probable evolution under the time-reversed driving protocol. We show that this bound can be understood as a macroscopic consequence of the fluctuation theorem: the time reverse of this evolution provides a possible fluctuation path under the forward dynamics. In the linear-response and slow-driving regime, the bound becomes an equality to first order and generalizes the McLennan-Zubarev formula to the time-dependent probability density of nonautonomous systems with weak nonconservative affinities. We illustrate our results in a bistable system under sudden quenches and periodic driving.
summary: This paper develops an Emergent Second Law for nonautonomous open quantum systems, providing a rigorous constraint on how macroscopic fluctuations evolve over time. By generalizing fluctuation theorems using large deviation theory, it establishes a bound on the rate function related to entropy production. This is significant because it offers a powerful, general thermodynamic tool to analyze non-equilibrium processes far from equilibrium.
main_problem: The paper derives an emergent second law that constrains time-dependent macroscopic fluctuations in nonautonomous open systems, generalizing existing fluctuation theorems.
main_result: A key inequality is established bounding the time-dependent rate function in terms of the entropy production along the most probable evolution under the time-reversed driving protocol.
method: The derivation utilizes large deviation theory, transforming the master equation into a Hamilton-Jacobi equation to establish the bound.
model_or_system: The analysis applies to general macroscopic stochastic systems described by continuous-time Markov jump processes, exemplified by systems with time-dependent potentials and rates.
key_observables: Rate function $I(c,t)$, Entropy Production (EP) rate $\langle\dot{\Sigma}angle$, and the macroscopic density $p(c,t)$.
important_parameters: Time-dependent driving protocols, linear-response/slow-driving regime, and the large-deviation limit ($V 	o \infty$).
main_assumptions: The derivation assumes the existence of a macroscopic limit and that the probability density follows the large-deviation form $p(c,t) \propto e^{-V I(c,t)}$.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the comparison between numerically calculated rate functions and the derived bounds for both instantaneous quenches and periodically driven systems.
paper_structure: The paper builds from the general stochastic master equation to the large-deviation form, derives the Hamilton-Jacobi equation, establishes the general bound (ESL), and then specializes this bound to the linear-response and slow-driving regimes.
why_interesting: This work provides a powerful, general thermodynamic constraint (the ESL) on non-equilibrium dynamics, which is crucial for understanding how systems relax or evolve under time-varying external fields, connecting fluctuation theorems to macroscopic observables.
